←Module 6: Gmail
Lesson · 20 min

Find Your Way Around Gmail

Learn the parts of the Gmail screen, how inbox tabs sort your mail, how stars and importance markers flag what matters, and when to archive a message instead of deleting it.

By the end of this lesson you can

  • ✓Name the main parts of Gmail on a computer: Compose, the main menu, Search mail, Settings, inbox tabs, and the side panel
  • ✓Explain what the Primary, Promotions, Social, Updates, and Forums tabs hold, move a message to another tab, and choose which tabs to show
  • ✓Flag messages with stars and importance markers, and find them again
  • ✓Decide whether to archive or delete a message, and find archived mail in All Mail and deleted mail in Trash

Lesson Notes

Read through the key concepts before you try the challenge.

Your new work inbox

On the job

You are the new office assistant at Parkview Property Management, a small company that manages apartment buildings.

On your first morning, Denise Carter, the office manager, tells you the whole office runs on Google Workspace: email in Gmail, schedules in Google Calendar, files in Google Drive, and meetings in Google Meet. When you open Gmail, there are already messages from coworkers, a plumbing company, the water utility, and a store you have never heard of.

Your task: Learn the Gmail screen well enough to sort a busy inbox in a few minutes.

Gmail is Google's email service. A personal Google Account has an address that ends in @gmail.com. A work or school account on Google Workspace uses the organization's own domain, such as jlee@parkviewpm.example. Either way, you use the same Gmail app in a web browser at mail.google.com, so what you practice here works for both.

Key terms

Google Workspace
Google's set of work apps (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Meet, Chat) that an organization manages for its people.
Conversation
A message and all of its replies, shown together. Gmail groups replies with the original message.
Inbox tabs (categories)
Primary, Promotions, Social, Updates, and Forums. Gmail sorts incoming mail into the tabs you turn on.
Archive
Removes a message from the inbox but keeps it. You can still find it in All Mail and by searching.
Trash
Where deleted messages go. You can recover them for up to 30 days; after that they are permanently deleted.
Star
A flag you add to a message so you can find it again under Starred.

The parts of the Gmail screen

💡 On a shared or public computer, sign out when you finish: select your profile picture or initial at the top right, then Sign out. Closing the tab can leave you signed in for the next person.

Inbox tabs sort mail for you

Gmail can sort incoming mail into tabs across the top of the inbox. Primary holds messages from people you know and anything that doesn't fit another tab. Promotions holds deals and offers. Social holds messages from social networks and media sites. Updates holds confirmations, receipts, bills, and statements. Forums holds messages from online groups and mailing lists. Gmail decides where each message goes, and you can correct it.

  1. To move a message to the right tab, drag it from the message list onto the tab. A notice appears at the bottom left with Undo in case you dropped it in the wrong place.
  2. To choose which tabs appear, select Settings (gear) at the top right. In Quick settings, under Inbox type, make sure Default is selected, then select Customize.
  3. Select one or more tabs (categories) and select Save at the bottom of the window. To turn tabs off completely, choose a different inbox type.

If you also use Outlook, the idea is similar to Outlook's Focused and Other tabs: the app sorts mail so the messages from people stand out. In Gmail you can have up to five tabs instead of two.

Stars and importance markers

A star is a flag you set yourself. To star a message, select the star to the left of it in the inbox, or open the message and select the star next to the date. Every starred message appears under Starred in the main menu, and you can search for is:starred.

The importance marker is the tag-shaped marker next to the star. Gmail fills it in yellow when it thinks a message matters, based on things like whom you email often and which messages you open and reply to. Select the marker to correct Gmail; that also teaches it what you consider important. Search for is:important to see every message marked important. If you don't want markers, go to Settings, See all settings, the Inbox tab, and choose No markers under Importance markers.

Archive or delete?

Archiving takes a message out of the inbox without deleting it. It stays in All Mail, it still shows up when you search, and if someone replies, the conversation comes back to your inbox. Use Archive (the box with a down arrow, or the E key) for anything you are done with but might need later: a confirmation, an FYI, a finished conversation.

Deleting moves a message to Trash. You can recover it for up to 30 days: open Trash (under More), check the message, select Move to, and choose where it goes. After 30 days it is permanently deleted. Use Delete for things you will never need, such as an expired sale.

Worked example

Clearing the inbox on your first morning

Get the Parkview inbox down to the messages that still need you.

  1. 1

    Open the Promotions tab and delete the printer paper sale.

    A sale email has no business value later, so it can go to Trash.

  2. 2

    Archive Kim's FYI about the pest control visit.

    It needs no action, but the office might need to know when the visit happened. Archive keeps it searchable.

  3. 3

    Star Denise's welcome message.

    It lists things to ask about this week, so you want to find it quickly under Starred.

  4. 4

    Leave Andre's showing message in the inbox.

    It still needs a reply. The inbox works best as a to-do list of what still needs you.

Result: The inbox holds only conversations that need action, and nothing useful was thrown away.

🔑 Archive what you are done with; delete only what you will never need; star what you must come back to.

Challenge

Apply what you've learned in this lesson.

Practice in your own Gmail. Use a personal Google Account (you can create one for free at accounts.google.com) or your school account if it includes Gmail.

  1. Open Gmail at mail.google.com. Write down which inbox tabs you see across the top.
  2. Open Settings (gear) › Quick settings › Inbox type › Customize. Write down which tabs are checked, then select Cancel (or Save if you changed something on purpose).
  3. Star one message you want to come back to. Open Starred to see it.
  4. Archive one message you no longer need in the inbox. Then open More › All Mail and find it.
  5. Write two sentences: when you would archive a work message, and when you would delete one.
Deliverable: Submit your list of tabs, your two sentences, and a screenshot of the archived message in All Mail to your instructor or course folder. If you can't use Gmail on your computer, complete the practice simulation and submit its results page (Print or save results on the finish card).
